subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this umbrella remain the canonical tracker for multi-agent orchestration stability while focused PRs/issues handle subagent delivery and session-lock repairs, or should maintainers split and close it after choosing a narrower canonical issue?
rationale: Current main fixes only parts of the report, and the remaining symptoms span reliability bugs plus product choices around subagent completion shape, session ownership, and operator recovery.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Repairs
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical umbrella, land or close focused repairs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540, and require each fix to prove the relevant live path.

options.title: Promote A Narrow Canonical Issue
options.body: Choose one focused issue, such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92433 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89927, as the canonical remaining root cause and close this umbrella only after preserving its production evidence there.

options.title: Defer Heavy Orchestration Direction
options.body: Reject token-ring or manager-framework expansion for now and keep only narrow bug fixes aligned with current agent/session infrastructure.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Repairs
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical umbrella, land or close focused repairs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540, and require each fix to prove the relevant live path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and merge provenance connect steipete to the config, subagent, and session-lock surfaces, and the remaining choice is cross-cutting owner-boundary direction.
